C1.title: Add alternatives; multiply stages
paragraphs: Choosing one of 2 shirts and then one of 3 pairs of pants creates 2 × 3 = 6 outfits. Each shirt has three continuations.
If instead you choose one item from 2 shirts or 3 pairs of pants, the alternatives are disjoint: there are 2 + 3 = 5 choices. Check what one completed outcome contains before deciding how to count.

C5.title: Count three-digit numbers containing a zero
paragraphs: There are 9 × 10 × 10 = 900 three-digit numbers. The first digit cannot be zero.
There are 9 × 9 × 9 = 729 with no zero anywhere. Subtract this complement: 900 − 729 = 171 contain at least one zero.

N4.title: See why 72 has twelve positive divisors
paragraphs: Write 72 = 2³ × 3². Each positive divisor chooses an exponent for 2 from 0, 1, 2, 3 and an exponent for 3 from 0, 1, 2.
These independent choices give 4 × 3 = 12 divisors. Each exponent pair produces exactly one divisor.

F1.title: Estimate before calculating
paragraphs: For 198 × 5, estimate with 200 × 5 = 1000. The exact product should be slightly smaller.
Subtract the two extra groups of five: 1000 − 10 = 990. The estimate helps you catch an answer with the wrong size.

C4.title: Make cases that cover every outcome once
paragraphs: Count two-digit numbers using only 1 and 2. Separate the cases by the tens digit: 11 and 12 begin with 1; 21 and 22 begin with 2.
Every allowed number belongs to exactly one case. The two cases contribute 2 + 2 = 4 numbers, with no overlap and nothing missing.

G4.title: Subtract a missing area
paragraphs: An 8-by-5 rectangle has area 40 square units. Removing a 3-by-2 rectangle from one corner removes 6 square units.
The remaining L-shaped region has area 40 − 6 = 34 square units. Label a decomposition so that its pieces neither overlap nor leave gaps.
